description: A TypeScript client for trip planning, stop departures, and single-trip lookups over the Spider transit API — one typed client that ships the allowed queries and attaches auth for you, with zero runtime dependencies.
rules: Construct one client with `new SpiderClient(baseUrl, apiKey)`, where `baseUrl` is the per-environment host `https://your-env-slug.api.tiducto.eu` and the key is sent in an `apikey` header scoped to a single project and environment. All three surfaces — `client.routing`, `client.stops`, `client.realtime` — are ready immediately; there is no install step. Use the literal placeholders `your-env-slug` and `your-api-key` in examples.

Plan a trip with `client.routing.plan({ origin, destination, departAt, searchWindowMinutes })`, building each endpoint via `Location.coordinate(lat, lon)` or `Location.stop(id)`. Page results with `planNext`/`planPrevious`, or stream itineraries with `planStream({ origin, destination, targetResults, maxWindowMinutes })` (both required, `maxWindowMinutes` at least 120); other routing calls are `departures(...)` for a stop's upcoming departures and `trip(tripId)` for a single trip's stops and times.

Every call returns a `SpiderResult<T>`, a discriminated union on `isSuccess` — branch on it, then read `data` or `error` instead of relying on exceptions. `error.code` is one of network, timeout, unauthorized, bad_request, not_found, query_retired, planning_limit_reached, agreement_inactive, server, rate_limited, decoding, unknown; `bad_request` names the invalid input in `error.field`, `query_retired` means the API no longer serves that persisted query, `planning_limit_reached` means the project has reached the trip planning limit its plan includes, and `agreement_inactive` means the project has no active agreement. Enum values the SDK doesn't know decode to 'UNKNOWN'.

`client.stops` offers text/autocomplete `search` (matching name, code, town and district; filter by `modes`; `limit` 1–50, default 20), lookup by GTFS id via `byId`, and geo queries `near(lat, lng)` / `within(bbox)`. `client.realtime` is poll-based with no push connections — call `vehicles`, `vehicleForTrip`, `delays`, or `alerts` on an interval and read `freshness` on each snapshot.
